cases.sentence: Она стояла в своей комнате над ___, отбирая вещи, когда он, уже одетый, раньше обыкновенного вошел к ней.
cases.explain: «открытым сундуком» — after the preposition «над», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Feeling that the reconciliation was complete, Anna set eagerly to work in the morning preparing for their departure. Though it was not settled whether they should go on Monday or Tuesday, as they had each given way to the other, Anna packed busily, feeling absolutely indifferent whether they went a day earlier or later. She was standing in her room over an open box, taking things out of it, when he came in to see her earlier than usual, dressed to go out.

cases.sentence: Иди в столовую, я сейчас приду, только отобрать эти ___, – сказала она, передавая на руку Аннушки, на которой уже лежала гора тряпок, еще что-то.
cases.explain: «ненужные вещи» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “No, I shan’t be ready by then myself,” she said; and at once reflected, “so then it was possible to arrange to do as I wished.” “No, do as you meant to do. Go into the dining-room, I’m coming directly. It’s only to turn out those things that aren’t wanted,” she said, putting something more on the heap of frippery that lay in Annushka’s arms.

cases.sentence: – Ясность не в форме, а в любви, – сказала она, все более и более раздражаясь не словами, а тоном ___, с которым он говорил. – Для чего ты желаешь этого?
cases.explain: «холодного спокойствия» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Definiteness is not in the form but the love,” she said, more and more irritated, not by his words, but by the tone of cool composure in which he spoke. “What do you want it for?”

cases.sentence: Более всего для тебя, – морщась, точно от боли, повторил он, – потому что я уверен, что ___ твоего раздражения происходит от неопределенности положения.
cases.explain: «бóльшая доля» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, I said: for your sake. Above all for your sake,” he repeated, frowning as though in pain, “because I am certain that the greater part of your irritability comes from the indefiniteness of the position.”

cases.sentence: Пристально глядя на него, на его лицо, руки, она вспоминала со всеми подробностями сцену ___ и его страстные ласки.
cases.explain: «вчерашнего примирения» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: She did not answer. Looking intently at him, at his face, his hands, she recalled all the details of their reconciliation the previous day, and his passionate caresses. “There, just such caresses he has lavished, and will lavish, and longs to lavish on other women!” she thought.

cases.sentence: «Эти, точно такие же ласки он расточал и будет и хочет расточать ___!» – думала она.
cases.explain: «другим женщинам» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: She did not answer. Looking intently at him, at his face, his hands, she recalled all the details of their reconciliation the previous day, and his passionate caresses. “There, just such caresses he has lavished, and will lavish, and longs to lavish on other women!” she thought.

cases.sentence: Ведь мое все состояние тут, – он показал на боковой карман, – и теперь я ___; а нынче поеду в клуб и, может быть, выйду нищим.
cases.explain: «богатый человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I’ve never asked myself the question, Anna Arkadyevna, whether I’m sorry for him or not. You see, all my fortune’s here”—he touched his breast pocket—“and just now I’m a wealthy man. But today I’m going to the club, and I may come out a beggar. You see, whoever sits down to play with me—he wants to leave me without a shirt to my back, and so do I him. And so we fight it out, and that’s the pleasure of it.”

cases.sentence: Она хотела притвориться, что ищет что-нибудь на столе, но, устыдившись притворства, прямо взглянула ему в лицо ___.
cases.explain: «холодным взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Before leaving the house, Vronsky went into her room. She would have pretended to be looking for something on the table, but ashamed of making a pretense, she looked straight in his face with cold eyes.
